title: Anything With Geometry — Ink on Paper: the Pen-Plotter Loop
thesis: Fogleman's ln turns any 3D scene into hidden-line vector paths, and vpype makes those paths plotter-ready. Everything else in the catalog that produces geometry — a phone scan, a ripped PS1 level, a ray-marched fractal, a strange attractor, the phase-space shape of BTC volatility, a Blender scene an agent wrote in Python — becomes a source for that one pipe. The output is a physical ink original, and in a market drowning in free pixels that is the scarce thing.
why_it_matters: You get a repeatable way to make signed physical editions from subjects nobody else is drawing, with the agent doing the scene work and the plotter doing the craft. Print-on-demand and no-proposal grants already give you a path to sell and fund it.
novelty: The catalog has ln + vpype as a standalone tool post and the geometry sources as separate curiosities — nobody wires scans, game rips or market attractors into a plotter. The existing generative-art dive stays on screen; this one ends on paper.

action_sketch: Week 1: install ln (Go) and vpype; have Claude Code write a script that loads an OBJ (start with a DuckStation PS1 rip or a phone scan) into ln, sets camera and texture paths, and exports SVG; run vpype linemerge/linesort and preview

Week 2: add two math sources — a Thomas attractor and a 3-lag phase-space embedding of a year of BTC daily volatility — emitted as 3D polylines straight into ln; make a 6-print series titled by date range

Week 3: plot the series on an A3 pen plotter (AxiDraw-class or a DIY drawing machine) with two pen weights, photograph per the print-on-demand guide, list originals plus POD reproductions, and submit to one grant
Falsifier: if scanned or ripped meshes produce unreadable line mush unless you hand-pick every path, or if plotted originals cannot sell above the POD print price, the loop is a toy, not a practice
prerequisites: Pen plotter or a DIY drawing machine
Go toolchain for ln, Python for vpype

title: Capture the Room Twice — Splat Scans and Song for Roots Music
thesis: Roots musicians already treat the room as an instrument — testing a 200-year-old house's resonance, filming tunes on porches and in old venues, the way Lomax filmed singers in their own kitchens. A phone can now capture that room as a Gaussian splat, and Gausseous makes the splat react to audio in a browser. Record the room's acoustics in the same session and the sound and the image come from one capture of one place.
why_it_matters: A two-person act with a phone gets a music video format where the place itself moves with the tune — no crew, no generated faces, and the result is documentary, not synthetic. It also gives folk and field-recording traditions a native visual form instead of borrowing pop-video tropes.
novelty: Splat tools sit in the creative and AI collections; place-bound folk performance sits in music. Nobody in the catalog points one at the other, and the paired room-acoustic capture is absent everywhere.

action_sketch: Scan one meaningful room (a porch, a church, a barn) with a phone splat app (Polycam or Luma), then load the .ply into Gausseous and drive it with a rough recording of one tune
In the same session, record a clap or sine-sweep impulse response of the room and convolve your dry instrument recording with it, so the audio carries that room's acoustics
Cut a 60-second vertical piece — real performance footage intercut with the reacting splat — and A/B it against a plain performance video on the same account
Falsifier: if low-light interior scans come out too noisy to read, or the splat cut loses watch-through to the plain performance video, the format is a gimmick
prerequisites: A room with a story and permission to scan it

title: Escaping the AI House Style — Taste Trained on the Public Domain
thesis: Look at the design stacks in this catalog and the same names keep coming back: Impeccable, awesome-design-md, 21st.dev, Emil Kowalski skills. When everyone feeds their agent the same borrowed systems, AI-built work converges on one house style. The way out is the reference corpus — scrape a public-domain archive nobody is mining, like rave zines, arcade flyers, transit posters or historical maps, embed it, find your clusters, and compile them into a DESIGN.md and prompt profile only you hold.
why_it_matters: Distinctiveness moves from prompting skill to corpus ownership. A solo designer or studio gets a reproducible, defensible style the agent can hit every time, instead of polishing the same Impeccable output as everyone else.
novelty: One creator (rndyrbrts) is turning a personal moodboard into data, and separately the ai3 archive links sit unused as C-tier bookmarks. Nobody connects archive mining, embedding clusters and agent design files — the catalog's own design posts all borrow famous brands.

If the clusters hold, train a small image LoRA on the chosen cluster for hero imagery and wrap the whole thing as a Claude skill

title: One Dancer, a Thousand Bodies — Ensemble Choreography from Herd Physics
thesis: Crystal Pite's ensemble pieces make dozens of dancers move like one organism, and that takes a company and months of rehearsal. Now webcam mocap captures one dancer, text-to-motion models spin out variations, and the quant collection's Ising herding model supplies the missing rule: one temperature knob that moves a crowd from noise to sudden collective turns. That last step is a market model used here as a choreographic score.
why_it_matters: A solo dancer or animator can compose crowd choreography with real intention — not a boids screensaver — and render it with production cloth physics. It's a new kind of score: the choreographer sets coupling and temperature, and the dancer's signature motion spreads through the crowd.
novelty: Ensemble choreography, mocap, flocking and the Ising model sit in four different collections. The existing generative-art dive uses boids as pretty motion. Nobody uses phase transitions as a compositional device for human movement.

Have Claude write a Blender script: 200–1,000 instances on a lattice, each with an Ising spin (which phrase or facing to adopt) updated by neighbor coupling, plus boids spacing; expose temperature as a driver on a gamepad axis
Render a 90-second piece where you drop temperature through the critical point live, then add PPF cloth to a 50-body subset for the hero shot
Falsifier: if viewers describe it as a screensaver or particle effect rather than a crowd of people with intention, the herd score isn't carrying meaning
prerequisites: A dancer willing to be captured

title: The Album Is a Device Again — Offline Generative Music Objects
thesis: Tristan Perich already shipped a symphony as a chip in a CD case. Google's Gemma Translator shows a full speech model stack running offline on a Pi 5 with a printable case and parts list. Local voice cloning fits in 100M parameters, and memory LCDs sip power. Put those together and a song can be a small object that performs a slightly different take every time it plays — the artist's own voice and stems, recombined on device, forever, with no server.
why_it_matters: Musicians get a physical edition that streaming can't flatten — each object unique, each play unrepeatable — at a bill of materials a small run can carry. It turns a release back into something you own instead of license.
novelty: The catalog has the art reference (1-Bit Symphony), the hardware recipe (Pi translator, memory display, NFC triggers) and local audio models, but in separate music, creative and ai8 posts. No one in it proposes generative, on-device releases.

Add a local voice layer — Pocket TTS or a small cloned-voice model speaking or singing a variable spoken-word line — plus a memory LCD showing the play number and today's arrangement

Falsifier: if listeners in a blind test prefer the fixed studio take every time, or the BOM forces a price above what 10 fans will pay, the format is a curio

title: Melody Genealogy — Crate-Digging the Public Domain with Local Search
thesis: Chance McCoy traces Shady Grove back to Child Ballad #81 and Sally in the Garden to a 1929 Brunswick 78 — by ear, one tune at a time. Sample diggers do the same hunt for producer gold, also by hand. Local multimodal search like SentrySearch already finds moments in hours of video from a plain-language query. Point that pattern at Lomax, Prelinger and 78-rpm archives with audio embeddings, and you get a tune family tree plus cleared public-domain samples, each with provenance.
why_it_matters: Folk players, music teachers and producers get a searchable map of how melodies travelled across centuries, languages and continents. Producers get a legally clean sample source with a story attached — the opposite of crate-digging your way into a clearance fight.
novelty: The music collection is full of hand-done lineage work and lyric translations; the ai collections hold local video search and embedding research. Nobody connects them, and no entry treats the public domain as a searchable sample bank with provenance.
